summary.en-US: Records online meetings joined in Firefox (Teams, Google Meet, Zoom, Jitsi, Webex, any site) and sends them to the Koalino app on this computer, which transcribes them offline.

description.en-US:
Koalino is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0-or-later) meeting note-taker that transcribes and summarizes meetings on your own devices. This add-on records the calls you join in Firefox and hands them to it. It needs the Koalino desktop app (Linux or Windows) running on the same computer. The add-on talks only to that app, through Firefox's native messaging; it sends nothing to any other server. When a call starts on Teams, Google Meet, Zoom, Jitsi Meet, Webex or Whereby, it asks whether to record it (Record, Always here, Not now, Never here). On any other site, press Record this tab in its button, or turn on Watch every website for calls (it then asks for access to all sites). While it records, an indicator with a Stop button stays on the page. It sends to Koalino:
  • your microphone and the other participants' audio, for the transcript;
  • frames of shared slides and screens, once per slide (never cameras);
  • on Teams also the live captions (shown only to you) and the Teams transcript panel, for speaker names, and after the meeting the Teams transcript from the meeting chat's recap, when there is one.
Optional and off by default on Teams: start Teams transcription when you record, and set Teams' spoken language to Koalino's. Please tell the other participants that you are recording. It runs on the meeting sites above, on SharePoint frames that Teams opens to show a recap's transcript, on a tab you choose to record, and on every site only if you allow it.

version.approval_notes:
Build from the attached source: Node.js 20 or newer, then `npm ci` and `node build.mjs` in the source folder. The Firefox build is written to dist/firefox (esbuild bundles the TypeScript entry points; nothing is minified).

The add-on needs the Koalino desktop app, which provides the native messaging host `com.note_taker.browser_bridge` (registered by `browser-host install`). Without it, the popup says Koalino is not reachable and nothing is recorded. All captured data goes only to that local host; the add-on makes no network requests of its own.

The page script (hook.js) runs in the meeting sites' pages (Teams, Google Meet, Zoom, Jitsi, Webex, Whereby) to see whether the page is in a WebRTC call and, after the user chooses Record, to tap the call's audio tracks (the user's microphone and the remote audio) and read frames of a shared screen. On SharePoint it runs only in frames a Teams page opened, to copy the recap transcript download. On other sites it runs only in a tab the user records with the popup's Record this tab (activeTab and scripting), or on every https site after the user turns on Watch every website for calls, which requests the optional host permission https://*/* first.
